title: Return Values
concept: The return statement sends a value back from a function. A function's return type declares what kind of value it produces.
why: Functions compute and give back results. Without return values, functions would be one-way — they couldn't produce output.
syntax_ref: return value;  // sends value back and exits function
tips: `return` both produces a value AND exits the function immediately
The return type (`-> Int`) is a PROMISE — the function must deliver
You can return any expression: `return a + b * c;`
A function with `-> Int` must return an Int on EVERY code path
common_mistakes: Forgetting `return` — just writing `x + y;` doesn't send the value back
Return type mismatch: declaring `-> Int` but returning a Str
Having code after `return` that never executes (dead code)
